3. Data Preprocessing¶

In [ ]:
# 3.1 Standardise Target variable
data['Churn'] = data['Churn'].str.strip().str.capitalize()
print("Churn after normalisation:\n", data['Churn'].value_counts())

Churn after normalisation:
 Churn
No     8650
Yes    3405
Name: count, dtype: int64
In [ ]:
# 3.2 Clean MonthlyCharges & TotalCharges
for col in ['MonthlyCharges', 'TotalCharges']:
    data[col] = data[col].astype(str).str.replace('$', '', regex=False).str.strip()
    data[col] = pd.to_numeric(data[col].replace('nan', np.nan), errors='coerce')

# 3.3 Anomalous tenure
anomalous_tenure = (data['tenure'] < 0).sum()
print(f"Anomalous tenure rows (negative): {anomalous_tenure}")
data.loc[data['tenure'] < 0, 'tenure'] = np.nan

# 3.4 Remove duplicates
print(f"Duplicates before: {data.duplicated().sum()}")
data = data.drop_duplicates()
print(f"Duplicates after: {data.duplicated().sum()}")

# 3.5 Standardise PaymentMethod
data['PaymentMethod'] = data['PaymentMethod'].str.strip().str.title()
print("\nPaymentMethod unique values:\n", data['PaymentMethod'].unique())

# 3.6 Missing value summary
print("\nMissing values per column:")
print(data.isnull().sum()[data.isnull().sum() > 0])

# 3.7 Impute missing values with median
data['tenure'].fillna(data['tenure'].median(), inplace=True)
data['MonthlyCharges'].fillna(data['MonthlyCharges'].median(), inplace=True)
data['TotalCharges'].fillna(data['TotalCharges'].median(), inplace=True)
print("\nMissing values after imputation:", data.isnull().sum().sum())

In [ ]:
# 3.8 Outlier Check & Treatment (IQR)
numeric_cols = ['tenure', 'MonthlyCharges', 'TotalCharges']
print("\n=== OUTLIER ANALYSIS (IQR Method) ===")
for col in numeric_cols:
    Q1  = data[col].quantile(0.25)
    Q3  = data[col].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    n_outliers = ((data[col] < lower) | (data[col] > upper)).sum()
    print(f"{col}: Q1={Q1:.2f}, Q3={Q3:.2f}, IQR={IQR:.2f}, "
          f"Lower={lower:.2f}, Upper={upper:.2f}, Outliers={n_outliers}")

=== OUTLIER ANALYSIS (IQR Method) ===
tenure: Q1=8.00, Q3=53.00, IQR=45.00, Lower=-59.50, Upper=120.50, Outliers=0
MonthlyCharges: Q1=35.45, Q3=88.80, IQR=53.35, Lower=-44.57, Upper=168.82, Outliers=0
TotalCharges: Q1=505.95, Q3=3548.02, IQR=3042.07, Lower=-4057.15, Upper=8111.11, Outliers=77

# Before capping plots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4))
for ax, col, color in zip(axes, numeric_cols, [GREEN, OAK, YELLOW]):
    ax.boxplot(data[col].dropna(), patch_artist=True,
               boxprops=dict(facecolor=color, alpha=0.7),
               medianprops=dict(color=RUST, linewidth=2))
    ax.set_title(f'{col} – Before Capping')
    ax.set_ylabel(col)
plt.suptitle('Outlier Detection – Before IQR Capping', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('fig_outlier_before.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()
In [ ]:
# IQR Capping (Winsorisation)
for col in numeric_cols:
    Q1  = data[col].quantile(0.25)
    Q3  = data[col].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    data[col] = data[col].clip(lower=lower, upper=upper)

# Fix negative TotalCharges after capping
data['TotalCharges'] = data['TotalCharges'].clip(lower=0)

print("\nAfter IQR capping — descriptive stats:")
print(data[numeric_cols].describe().round(2))

4. Exploratory Data Analysis¶

4.1 Target Distribution¶

In [ ]:
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
sns.countplot(data=data, x='Churn', palette={'No': GREEN, 'Yes': RUST}, ax=ax, edgecolor='black')
ax.set_title('Overall Churn Distribution', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Customers')
ax.set_xlabel('Churn Status')
total = len(data)
for p in ax.patches:
    count = int(p.get_height())
    pct   = f'{100 * count / total:.1f}%'
    ax.annotate(f'{count}\n({pct})',
                (p.get_x() + p.get_width()/2, p.get_height()),
                ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold',
                xytext=(0, 5), textcoords='offset points', color=RUST)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('fig1_churn_dist.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

5. Feature Engineering & Final Preprocessing¶

# Encode categoricals

data_enc = data_enc.dropna()

print(f"Class distribution:\n{data_enc['Churn_bin'].value_counts()}")

7. Feature Scaling¶

In [ ]:

In [ ]:
def evaluate_model(name, model, X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test):
    """Evaluate model on both train and test set and return metrics."""
    y_train_pred  = model.predict(X_train)
    y_train_proba = model.predict_proba(X_train)[:, 1]
    y_test_pred   = model.predict(X_test)
    y_test_proba  = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

    metrics = {
        'Model'          : name,
        'Train Accuracy' : round(accuracy_score(y_train, y_train_pred), 4),
        'Test Accuracy'  : round(accuracy_score(y_test, y_test_pred), 4),
        'Train Precision': round(precision_score(y_train, y_train_pred), 4),
        'Test Precision' : round(precision_score(y_test, y_test_pred), 4),
        'Train Recall'   : round(recall_score(y_train, y_train_pred), 4),
        'Test Recall'    : round(recall_score(y_test, y_test_pred), 4),
        'Train F1'       : round(f1_score(y_train, y_train_pred), 4),
        'Test F1'        : round(f1_score(y_test, y_test_pred), 4),
        'Train ROC-AUC'  : round(roc_auc_score(y_train, y_train_proba), 4),
        'Test ROC-AUC'   : round(roc_auc_score(y_test, y_test_proba), 4),
    }

    print(f"\n{'='*55}")
    print(f"  {name}")
    print(f"{'='*55}")
    print(f"{'Metric':<18} {'Train':>10} {'Test':>10}  {'Overfit?':>10}")
    print(f"{'-'*55}")
    for metric in ['Accuracy', 'Precision', 'Recall', 'F1', 'ROC-AUC']:
        train_val = metrics[f'Train {metric}']
        test_val  = metrics[f'Test {metric}']
        diff      = train_val - test_val
        flag      = 'Overfit' if diff > 0.05 else 'OK'
        print(f"{metric:<18} {train_val:>10.4f} {test_val:>10.4f}  {flag:>10}")

    print(f"\nTest Classification Report:")
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_test_pred,
                                target_names=['No Churn', 'Churned']))
    return metrics

}

all_metrics = [lr_metrics]   # start with baseline
results = {}                 # keep this for backward compatibility with ROC/CM plots below

for name, model in models.items():
    model.fit(X_res_sc, y_res)
    m = evaluate_model(name, model, X_res_sc, y_res, X_test_sc, y_test)
    all_metrics.append(m)
    results[name] = {
        'Accuracy' : m['Test Accuracy'],
        'Precision': m['Test Precision'],
        'Recall'   : m['Test Recall'],
        'F1 Score' : m['Test F1'],
        'ROC-AUC'  : m['Test ROC-AUC'],
    }

results_df = pd.DataFrame(results).T
summary_df = pd.DataFrame(all_metrics).set_index('Model')

print("\n=== ALL MODELS – TRAIN vs TEST SUMMARY ===")
print(summary_df.to_string())

        'ROC-AUC'  : m['Test ROC-AUC'],
    }

tuned_df = pd.DataFrame(tuned_results).T
tuned_summary_df = pd.DataFrame(tuned_metrics).set_index('Model')

print("\n=== TUNED MODELS – TRAIN vs TEST SUMMARY ===")
print(tuned_summary_df.to_string())

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
colors_tuned = [GREEN, RUST, OAK]
for (name, model), color in zip(tuned_models.items(), colors_tuned):
    y_proba_t = model.predict_proba(X_test_sc)[:, 1]
    fpr_t, tpr_t, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_proba_t)
    auc_t = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba_t)
    ax.plot(fpr_t, tpr_t, lw=2.5, color=color, label=f'{name} (AUC={auc_t:.3f})')
ax.plot([0,1],[0,1], 'k--', lw=1.5, label='Random Classifier')
ax.set_xlabel('False Positive Rate')
ax.set_ylabel('True Positive Rate')
ax.set_title('ROC Curves – Tuned Models', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(loc='lower right')
